Operator: Good day, and welcome to the CyberGuard Solutions Q2 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Jamie Patel, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Jamie Patel: Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss CyberGuard Solutions' results for the Q2 FY2024. With me on today's call are Alex Ramirez, Chief Executive Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Jordan Lee, Chief Technology Officer, and Maria Chen, Chief Security Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Ramirez.

Alex Ramirez: Thank you, Jamie, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us. CyberGuard Solutions had an exceptional Q2, exceeding expectations across all key metrics. We are seeing significant traction with our cloud-native security platform and are benefiting from the increased focus on cybersecurity across all industries. The impact of our new AI-powered threat detection, NeuroShield, is evident in the reduced incident response times reported by our customers, with many achieving sub-15-minute mean time to respond in real-world deployments.

Our strategy is centered around five core pillars: accelerating platform adoption through larger average deal sizes for new and existing customers, delivering exceptional customer feedback on our innovative products and features, fueling innovation with substantial R&D investments, expanding through our high-performing channel partners, and providing clear visibility via next-quarter billings guidance.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Elena Vasquez to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Alex. As Alex highlighted, we had a remarkable Q2. Revenue reached $638 million, reflecting a 32% year-over-year increase. This growth was fueled by both new customer acquisition and expansion within our existing customer base. Our gross margin remained strong at 78%, demonstrating our ability to scale efficiently. Operating expenses were $420 million, and net income was $150 million, translating to $0.85 per share. We are increasing our guidance for the full year based on these outstanding results.

Let me dive deeper into some key performance indicators starting with average deal size, or ADS, segmented by new and existing customers. In the cybersecurity industry, ADS serves as a critical leading indicator of our platform adoption, customer stickiness, and long-term revenue quality. We measure it primarily on an Annual Contract Value basis for initial deals, excluding professional services to emphasize our recurring SaaS revenue streams. This metric captures not only our pricing power but also the breadth of our platform, which includes endpoint detection and response, secure access service edge, cloud workload protection, and our GenAI Security Posture Management module.

For Q2 ended June 30th, our overall weighted average deal size came in at $385,000 in ACV, marking a robust 22% year-over-year increase and a 9% sequential quarter-over-quarter uptick. This outperforms industry benchmarks from peers like CrowdStrike, Zscaler, and Palo Alto Networks, where blended ADS growth has been around 15-18% year-over-year amid moderating post-pandemic momentum.

By customer cohort, new customers saw ADS reach $465,000, up 28% year-over-year from $363,000 in Q2 FY2023. This strong growth is driven by a shift toward large-enterprise land-and-expand motions, with new logos bundling our FalconX platform with SASE equivalents and our AI-driven autonomous EDR, pushing beyond standalone solutions. Year-to-date, new logo ADS is $452,000, with 65% of these deals now multi-product, up from 48% last year.

For existing customers, including expansions and renewals, ADS was $312,000, a solid 17% year-over-year increase. This ties into our industry-leading 128% net revenue retention in Q2, driven by upsells in zero-trust architecture and ransomware resilience modules. Notably, 42% of expansions included our GSPM add-on, which protects generative AI workloads from prompt injection and data exfiltration risks as enterprises adopt tools like ChatGPT Enterprise and custom LLMs.

These figures exclude one-off perpetual licenses, which we phased out two years ago in favor of subscription models, now making up over 95% of our SaaS revenue mix.

Key trends include platformization, where customers consolidate vendors to combat alert fatigue and skills gaps—our deals average 4.2 modules per customer, up from 3.1 year-over-year, with integrations into hyperscalers like AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, and Google Vertex AI. For example, a Q2 win with a Fortune 50 financial services firm started at $1.2 million ACV, layering EDR, SASE, and GSPM from day one. Multi-year contracting is also rising, with 72% of Q2 deals at three-plus years and total contract value averaging $1.45 million per deal, providing visibility into our $4.2 billion ARR runway.

Our NeuroShield AI engine, autonomously hunting stealthy advanced persistent threats with 99.2% true positive rates validated by MITRE ATT&CK evaluations, has accelerated deals. We've also introduced Zero-Trust Everywhere, a unified policy engine spanning OT/IoT, public cloud, and SaaS apps, resonating after incidents like Log4Shell and MOVEit breaches.

Regionally, North America, 72% of Q2 bookings, had $410,000 ADS, up 25% year-over-year, boosted by CMMC 2.0, SEC cyber disclosure rules, and NIST 2.0—such as a Big Four bank expansion from $800,000 to $2.1 million TCV. EMEA, 18% of bookings, saw $360,000 ADS, up 19%, driven by GDPR and NIS2, with wins in Germany and France 30% higher via sovereign cloud integrations. APAC, 10% of bookings, exploded to $315,000 ADS, up 35%, favored by India's DPDP Act and Australia's reforms, including six seven-figure deals like a Singapore telco bundling 5G/IoT security.

Looking ahead, we expect 20-25% year-over-year ADS growth for FY2024, outpacing Gartner's 12% CAGR for endpoint security through 2027, supported by our Secure-by-Design ecosystem—co-sell wins with AWS, Microsoft, and ServiceNow now 35% of pipeline—and mid-market channels via TD SYNNEX. Pricing pressure from open-source like Falco is mitigated by our 40% false positive reduction via federated learning, maintaining premiums amid 92% gross margins on expansions. This ADS expansion validates our flywheel: larger deals boost NRR, fueling 32% year-over-year ARR growth to $3.8 billion, positioning us as the control plane for enterprise resilience against quantum threats and AI-augmented attacks.

Next, I'd like to highlight our R&D investment, a key competitive moat in an industry where threats evolve faster than ever—think AI-powered polymorphic malware and nation-state quantum decryption attempts. For Q2, R&D totaled $148 million, or 23.2% of revenue, up 160 basis points year-over-year from 21.6%. This is up sequentially from Q1's 22.8%, reflecting hires of over 250 AI/ML specialists and our new Tel Aviv Quantum Security Lab. Trailing 12-month, we're at 22.5%, above the peer average of 19.2% per Gartner's magic quadrant, exceeding Palo Alto at 20%, matching CrowdStrike at 22%, and topping Zscaler at 18%.

The increase aligns with a 47% year-over-year surge in ransomware variants per our CyberGuard Threat Index. First, 35% of R&D, or $52 million, enhances FalconX EDR with generative AI for real-time behavioral anomaly detection, trained on 15 petabytes of telemetry from 8,500 customers, reducing MTTR to APTs by 42% in pilots with a major U.S. bank, ahead of Elastic SIEM and rivaling Darktrace.

Second, 26% or $38 million goes to Secure Access Edge SASE platform, integrating SWG, CASB, ZTNA with post-quantum cryptography like Kyber and Dilithium to counter harvest-now-decrypt-later attacks from APT41. This drives 28% year-over-year revenue in APAC via NTT and SoftBank partnerships amid supply chain attacks.

Third, 39% supports M&A from ThreatShield AI acquisition and XDR interoperability with Microsoft Sentinel and AWS Security Hub, with 15% more to EMEA—now 22% of spend—for NIS2 and GDPR, hiring 80 engineers in Dublin and Munich, yielding 36% quarter-over-quarter ARR growth there versus 29% in North America.

For full-year FY2024, expect 22-24% of revenue, trending higher if quantum needs escalate, versus 21.4% last year on $2.1 billion revenue. While pressuring near-term margins—non-GAAP operating at 28%—it's accretive long-term, correlating to our 32% five-year CAGR like CrowdStrike's. This fuels IP with 47 Q2 patents, attracts talent with 85 employee NPS, and avoids commoditization unlike legacy players below 18%.

Before moving on, customer feedback on our new products and features is a leading indicator for our $3.8 billion ARR, up 32% year-over-year. Through Voice of the Customer programs, NPS surveys, and executive business reviews, feedback is overwhelmingly positive amid threats like LockBit ransomware and APTs in Kubernetes. Enterprise NPS hit 78, up 12 points year-over-year, topping CrowdStrike's 75 and Palo Alto's 72 per Evergreen and G2. Gross dollar retention is 98%, NRR 125%, churn under 2% for top 500 logos. In surveys of 1,200-plus respondents, 92% rated new releases exceeding expectations for time-to-value and multi-cloud integration with AWS EKS, Azure AKS, Google Anthos.

Our Nexus AI Guardian XDR, layering generative AI on EDR for autonomous hunting, has 67% adoption across 3,500 customers, 85% of early adopters expanding 35%. GlobalBank noted it neutralized a zero-day Log4Shell variant missed by others, saving $2.5 million; users report 40% fewer false positives than Splunk, 3.2 times more insider threats flagged, 55% orchestration boost with Demisto and Swimlane.

Nexus Secure Access SASE 2.0, converging ZTNA, SWG, CASB, DLP, has 52% penetration, 142% NER for users, NPS 82. Customers praise 10 Gbps throughput, sub-50ms latency; an automotive firm said it blocked 97% phishing on OT/IoT versus Zscaler's 92%, strong with Okta integrations for FIDO2 MFA at 91% activation.

Quantum-Resistant Cryptography preview in Nexus Vault scores 89/100, 76% planning Q1 2025 migration, 25% faster key rotation for financials and healthcare against Salt Typhoon.

North America (62% ARR) leads with 81 NPS on AI Guardian, CISA-driven. EMEA excels in SASE at 65% penetration for NIS2/GDPR. APAC at 48% adoption but strong QRC feedback against Lazarus. LatAm grows fastest at 55% year-over-year ARR, NPS 76 for SMBs.

This validates our $450 million R&D—38% of revenue—on agentless deployment, GenAI copilots predicting 68% breaches pre-exploitation per red-teams. 84% shift from legacy like Check Point to our XDR/SASE; wins up 15% QoQ vs. SentinelOne, 22% vs. Netskope on 99.999% uptime. Q4 betas for AI deception and serverless security per VoC position us in $200 billion market.

Our channel partners are another growth engine. In Q2, they drove 42% of revenue, $285 million out of $638 million, up from 38% prior and 35% year-over-year, with channel growing 32% versus 22% direct. Trailing 12-month, $1.05 billion or 40% of $2.62 billion run-rate, 78% recurring, 118% channel NRR.

Distributors like Ingram Micro, TD Synnex, Arrow contributed 55% or $157 million, up 28%, with $450,000 ACV mid-market bundles of FalconSense AI EDR. VARs like CDW, SHI added 30% or $85 million, up 25%, via CyberShield Partner Accelerator with 2x SPIFFs on $1 million-plus contracts.

MSSPs/MSPs at 15% or $43 million, up 52%, via Optiv, Deloitte, BT Security on MDR with CyberXDR API; 65% MDR deals through them after training 1,200 engineers on quantum modules.

Americas (62%, $177 million, +29%) leverage CISA zero-trust, Colonial Pipeline lessons—a $25 million DoD deal with Presidio. EMEA ($68 million, 24%, +38%) bundles DLP for NIS2/GDPR with Computacenter, Bechtle at 45% attach. APAC (14%, $40 million, +25%) with NTT, Dimension Data for SASE on AWS Outposts.

Partner Fusion Lab certified 4,200 partners, up 40%, for SIEM/SOAR/GenAI integrations reducing false positives 40%; $50 million MDF prioritizes AWS/Azure co-sell, 22% pipeline. Expect 45% FY2025 revenue or $1.4 billion from 6,000 partners, mid-30s growth despite risks, with partner NPS 72, 95% renewals topping peers.

Finally, for Q3 billings guidance, a key indicator of subscription momentum, we guide $528 million to $538 million, 28% to 31% year-over-year growth, accelerating from Q2's 26%, sequential 4-6% from $512 million, reflecting enterprise ramps and multi-year front-loading.

Core platforms Quantum Endpoint Defender EDR and SecureAccess Cloud SASE drive this: QED over 40% year-over-year on AI malware demand, ACV to $1.2 million bundling Quantum XDR. SAC 35% growth, including $75 million hyperscaler deal akin to Zscaler integrations.

DBNRR at 118%, 65% billings from expansions like CWPP (50% growth last quarter). New logos 35%, 28% pipeline conversion via channels. Americas ~60%, federal CMMC deals. EMEA 35% growth on GDPR/ransomware, 15 euro-10 million-plus Quantum Ransomware Shield. APAC 20% mix, 45% growth on Singapore Act, Australia Eight, Tokyo DC.

Initiatives: GenAI Threat Intelligence 5% bookings, converged fabrics 20% win rates, Nebula Intercept M&A adding $20 million. Macro caution on SMBs offset by 95% retention; geopolitics boosts inquiries. RPO $4.2 billion, up 32%, current 42%. Positions us for IDC's 13% CAGR.

Next, Dr. Jordan Lee will provide more technical details.

Dr. Jordan Lee: Thank you, Elena. We continue to innovate and push the boundaries of what's possible in cybersecurity. Our team is focused on developing cutting-edge solutions that address the evolving threat landscape. We are investing heavily in research and development to stay ahead of the curve and deliver unparalleled value to our customers. Key areas of focus include advancing our NeuroShield AI for zero-day prediction, enhancing SASE convergence with post-quantum crypto, and ensuring seamless XDR interoperability across ecosystems—directly supporting the R&D intensity Elena outlined and the customer feedback on faster MTTR and fewer false positives.

Maria Chen: Thank you. Cybersecurity is paramount, and we are taking proactive measures to protect our customers and ourselves. We are committed to maintaining the highest standards of security and compliance, from NIST-aligned zero-trust implementations to rapid response against emerging threats like AI-augmented ransomware and supply chain exploits, as evidenced by our MITRE-validated detections and regional sovereignty features.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator: Instructions for Q&A session. At this time, to ask a question, please press star one. First question comes from Mike Donovan with Goldman Sachs.

Mike Donovan: Thanks. Elena, great detail on ADS—impressive new logo growth. Can you talk about sustainability given macro headwinds and how multi-year deals factor into FY24 outlook?

Elena Vasquez: Thanks, Mike. Sustainability comes from platformization and technical wins like NeuroShield, with 72% multi-year deals locking $1.45 million TCV average. We've offset budget delays with 92% expansion margins and channel co-sells at 35% pipeline. ADS growth of 20-25% holds for FY24.

Operator: Next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Chen: Elena, on customer feedback, the NPS jump is strong—any specifics on competitive displacement in SASE and XDR?

Elena Vasquez: Absolutely, Lisa. In EBRs, 15% QoQ wins over SentinelOne in EDR bake-offs and 22% versus Netskope in SASE POCs, thanks to 99.999% uptime and single-console. Automotive clients highlighted 97% phishing block on OT versus peers' 92%, with 84% shifting from legacy perimeter tools.

Operator: Next question comes from Raj Patel with JPMorgan.

Raj Patel: For Dr. Lee or Elena, how is R&D translating to ROI, especially AI/ML hires and quantum lab?

Dr. Jordan Lee: Raj, the $52 million in AI/ML has delivered 42% MTTR reduction in pilots, 68% pre-exploitation predictions per red-teams. Quantum lab supports PQC integrations preempting APT41, yielding EMEA ARR acceleration and 47 Q2 patents—clear ROI on our 23.2% intensity above peers.

Operator: Next question comes from Sarah Kim with Barclays.

Sarah Kim: Elena, channels at 42%—any color on MSSP growth and FY25 ramp risks?

Elena Vasquez: Sarah, MSSPs up 52% to 15% mix via 1,200 trained engineers on MDR APIs, 65% deals through them. FY25 target 45% or $1.4 billion from 6,000 partners, risks like supply chains mitigated by 72 partner NPS and hyperscaler focus—outpacing peers.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time.

Alex Ramirez: Thank you all for your insightful questions. We are confident in our ability to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. Thank you to our dedicated employees, loyal customers, and valued partners.

Jamie Patel: Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our call. You may now disconnect.
